photo_note: Photos are Wikimedia Commons thumbnails (hotlinked) with author and licence shown, or owner-supplied uploads in /assets/images with written permission. Never copy photos or data from other location databases; record only what a venue itself publishes, and keep source URLs.

locations.name: Bergisel Ski Jump
locations.setting: Zaha Hadid's 2002 ski jump tower on Innsbruck's Bergisel hill, combining a competition in-run and judging tower with a public viewing platform and cafe over the city.

locations.name: Erzberg
locations.setting: Open-pit iron ore mine near Eisenerz with terraced orange slopes over 700 metres high, a tourist park offering truck and cable tours through the workings, and host to the annual Erzbergrodeo enduro race.

locations.name: Gasometer Vienna
locations.setting: Four former 19th-century gasholders in Vienna's Simmering district, rebuilt with glass domes into apartments, offices, a shopping mall, cinema and event hall around their original brick shells.

locations.name: Hallstatt
locations.setting: Lakeside Alpine village of stacked wooden and stucco houses between the Hallstatter See and a steep mountainside, reachable by funicular to the salt mine above.

locations.name: Hangar-7
locations.setting: Curved glass and steel aviation hangar at Salzburg Airport housing the Flying Bulls historic aircraft collection, a restaurant and event spaces beneath its open-span dome roof.

locations.name: Hotel Sacher Vienna
locations.setting: Grand 1876 hotel opposite the State Opera, with red-panelled parlours, a chandeliered dining room and the original Sachertorte kitchen.

locations.name: Kirche am Steinhof (Klinik Penzing)
locations.setting: Otto Wagner's Art Nouveau hospital church of 1907 crowning a hillside campus of pavilion wards built for the former Lower Austrian asylum, now Vienna's Klinik Penzing.

locations.name: Kitzbühel
locations.setting: Alpine market town below the Hahnenkamm and Kitzbueheler Horn, with a pastel-fronted medieval centre and ski infrastructure running from the streets onto the pistes.

locations.name: Kunsthaus Graz
locations.setting: Biomorphic blue-panelled contemporary art museum of 2003 on the Mur riverbank, its bulging acrylic shell fitted with roof-top nozzle skylights beside Graz's baroque old town.

locations.name: Museum Arbeitswelt Steyr
locations.setting: Museum of industrial and labour history housed in a former weapons and bicycle factory hall in Steyr's Wehrgraben quarter, with original machine-hall interiors.

locations.name: Naschmarkt
locations.setting: A 1.5-kilometre open-air market along the Wienzeile with produce stalls, delicatessens and restaurants, and a Saturday flea market at its western end.

locations.name: Salzburg Old Town
locations.setting: Baroque old town of church domes, squares and narrow lanes beneath the Hohensalzburg fortress on the Salzach river.

locations.name: Schönbrunn Palace
locations.setting: Baroque imperial summer palace with more than 1,400 rooms, formal gardens, the Gloriette hilltop folly and a historic zoo.

locations.name: Semmering Railway
locations.setting: The world's first standard-gauge mountain railway, opened in 1854, still an operating OBB main line with sixteen tunnels and stone viaducts climbing the Semmering pass.

locations.name: Sölden
locations.setting: High Alpine ski resort village in the Ötztal valley with glacier roads climbing to 2,800 metres and a summit restaurant at 3,048 metres.

locations.name: Tabakfabrik Linz
locations.setting: A converted 1935 Bauhaus-style tobacco factory in Linz, now a creative and start-up quarter with exhibition halls, event spaces and a rooftop terrace across the Danube from the old town.

locations.name: University of Vienna Main Building
locations.setting: Historicist university building of 1884 on the Ringstrasse, with an arcaded courtyard of scholars' monuments, a grand ceremonial hall and lecture theatres.

locations.name: Vienna City Hall (Rathaus)
locations.setting: Neo-Gothic seat of Vienna's city government from 1883, with a vaulted arcaded courtyard, ceremonial halls and a square in front used for open-air events and markets.

locations.name: Vienna State Opera
locations.setting: An 1869 opera house on the Ringstrasse with a gilded auditorium, grand staircase and backstage areas that host around 350 performances a season.

locations.name: Wiener Riesenrad (Prater)
locations.setting: A 1897 giant Ferris wheel and adjoining amusement park on the edge of the Prater, with vintage gondola cabins and a fairground of rides, food stalls and an events hall.

locations.name: Wörthersee
locations.setting: A 19-kilometre subalpine lake ringed by resort towns, promenades, lidos and wooded hills between Klagenfurt and Velden.

locations.name: Abattoir, Anderlecht
locations.setting: Historic livestock market and food-hall complex in Anderlecht, Brussels, with weekend markets, the FOODMET food hall and renovated buildings used for events.

locations.name: Alden Biesen Castle
locations.setting: Moated former headquarters of the Teutonic Order in Bilzen with formal gardens and a museum, now a conference and cultural centre that lists availability for film shoots.
locations.suitability: Website lists availability for film shooting alongside conferences and events.

locations.name: Ancienne Belgique (AB)
locations.setting: Concert hall on Boulevard Anspach in central Brussels with two stages, offering the venue for private hire and running its own in-house production and photography team.

locations.name: Autoworld
locations.setting: Vintage and classic car museum in the Cinquantenaire park's Belvedere hall in Brussels, hired out as an event space for more than a thousand guests.
locations.facilities: Event space for over 1,000 guests among the car collection, with escape-game and audio-guide experiences.

locations.name: Bois du Cazier
locations.setting: Former coal mine at Marcinelle near Charleroi with preserved headframes and pithead buildings, site of the 1956 mining disaster, now housing industry and glass museums.

locations.name: Bozar
locations.setting: Centre for Fine Arts in central Brussels hosting concerts, exhibitions and film screenings across several halls, with a dedicated team for private and corporate venue hire.

locations.name: Bruges Historic Centre
locations.setting: Intact medieval city centre of canals, cobbled streets, stepped-gable brick houses and the towering thirteenth-century Belfry.

locations.name: C-mine
locations.setting: Former Winterslag coalmine in Genk with preserved headframes and a compressor hall, now a creative cluster of more than 30 spaces that are rented out for events.

locations.name: Château de Freÿr
locations.setting: Renaissance chateau on a bend of the Meuse near Hastière with terraced 18th-century gardens, whose barn and orangeries can be booked for events.

locations.name: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
locations.setting: Seven-kilometre motor racing circuit through the Ardennes hills near Francorchamps, host of the Formula 1 Belgian Grand Prix, with the track and facilities available to hire for private and business events.

locations.name: Citadel of Namur
locations.setting: Hilltop fortress complex above Namur spanning two thousand years of military building, with underground passages, a park and rooms offered for professional and private hire.

locations.name: Doel
locations.setting: Polder village on the Scheldt earmarked for demolition since the 1990s to expand the port of Antwerp, now with around 200 empty houses, street art and a small remaining community.

locations.name: Flagey
locations.setting: 1938 Art Deco former national radio building on Place Sainte-Croix in Brussels, now a music and cinema centre with studios and halls available for venue hire.

locations.name: Grand-Hornu
locations.setting: Neoclassical former colliery and workers' town near Mons, built 1810 to 1830 around an oval courtyard, now a design and contemporary art centre with rooms available for hire.

locations.name: Gravensteen
locations.setting: Moated twelfth-century stone castle with towers, battlements and a gatehouse standing in the middle of Ghent.

locations.name: Halles de Schaerbeek
locations.setting: Former covered market hall in Schaerbeek, Brussels, converted into a performing arts venue for dance and theatre, with its hall offered for hire.

locations.name: Handelsbeurs Concert Hall
locations.setting: 19th-century former merchants' exchange on the Kouter in Ghent, now a concert hall with a brasserie, offering its hall for private hire.

locations.name: Kortrijk Xpo
locations.setting: 40,000 square metre exhibition and conference campus in Kortrijk with six halls and a covered boulevard connecting them, rented out for trade shows, conferences and public events.
locations.facilities: Six halls, a Meeting Center with five rooms, catering, ticketing, parking and technical support.

locations.name: Kursaal Oostende
locations.setting: Seafront concert and congress hall in Ostend with a large auditorium and casino, offering dedicated business and corporate event spaces.

locations.name: La Monnaie / De Munt
locations.setting: Belgium's national opera house in central Brussels, offering venue hire and audiovisual exploitation services alongside its main stage and the smaller Malibran room.

locations.name: Lites Studios
locations.setting: Modern studio complex near Brussels with five stages, including Europe's largest heated indoor water tank for underwater filming.
locations.facilities: Five sound stages from 170 to 1,700 m2 (Stage 1: 1,250 m2, Stage 2: 1,700 m2) and a 1,450 m2 water stage with a 24 x 21 m deep section, up to 10.8 m depth with the floor flooded, 7 million litres kept at 30 to 32 C, a moveable pool floor rated for 20 tonnes of set and a 14.3 m grid height. Dressing rooms and an in-house camera rental department.
locations.suitability: Sound stages with high acoustic performance; the water stage is used for underwater and surface filming with a tilting, submersible platform and dual gantry cranes. The studio points to Belgium's 45 percent tax incentive.

locations.name: Loppem Castle
locations.setting: Neo-Gothic castle built in the 1850s and 1860s near Bruges with original interiors and art collections, whose former stables now form a hall for hire.
locations.facilities: Former stables converted into an event hall for 250 to 300 seated guests or 450 standing, plus vaulted cellars for smaller groups.

locations.name: Paleis op de Meir
locations.setting: 1745 rococo mansion on Antwerp's main shopping street, once refurbished for Napoleon Bonaparte, now a heritage house offering rooms for dinners, receptions and meetings.

locations.name: Saint Peter's Abbey, Ghent
locations.setting: Former Benedictine abbey by Sint-Pietersplein in Ghent with a baroque church, historic cellars and a south-facing vineyard garden, whose rooms are hired for receptions and conferences.
locations.facilities: Historic cellar and loft rooms, courtyard and south-facing garden with vineyard, underground parking nearby.

locations.name: Stoomcentrum Maldegem
locations.setting: Volunteer-run heritage railway based at Maldegem station, running historic steam and diesel trains through the Meetjesland countryside.
locations.suitability: Website explicitly offers photo and film location bookings alongside private charters and group visits.

locations.name: STUK, Leuven
locations.setting: Multidisciplinary arts centre on Naamsestraat in Leuven with theatre spaces, a cinema and studios, offering rooms and rehearsal spaces for rent.

locations.name: Tour & Taxis
locations.setting: Former customs and rail freight depot on the Brussels canal, with 19th-century brick, glass and iron warehouse halls now used as a large indoor event and exhibition venue.

locations.name: Villa Empain
locations.setting: 1930s Art Deco mansion on Avenue Franklin Roosevelt in Brussels, home to the Boghossian Foundation, with salons, gardens and a bar that can be privatised for events.

locations.name: Dubrovnik Old Town
locations.setting: Walled seaside old town with intact medieval ramparts, baroque stone streets and fortresses rising straight from the Adriatic.
locations.known_for: Game of Thrones (King's Landing, from season 2), Star Wars: The Last Jedi (2017), Robin Hood (2018)

locations.name: Jadran Film
locations.setting: Film studio founded in 1946 with stages and backlot grounds in Zagreb's Dubrava district, host to well over a hundred international co-productions.
locations.known_for: Winnetou series (1962-1968), The Tin Drum (1979), Sophie's Choice (1982)
locations.facilities: Nine stages totalling 8,000 m2; the largest are Studio 2 (1,200 m2, 47 x 23 m, over 10 m high) and Studio 4 (1,200 m2, 60 x 20 m, 8 m working height), with Studio 6-7 a divisible 950 m2 complex and Studio 9 a 440 m2 TV studio. A 1,000 m2 production hub with offices and its own transformer station, plus carpentry, paint, plaster and model workshops.
locations.suitability: Presented as a full-service production base with base camp infrastructure and dressing, makeup and wardrobe rooms around each stage; Studios 4 and 9 are on long-term lease to a television company and a 2,500 to 3,200 m2 Studio 10 is planned. Stage pages are marked under construction pending a summer 2026 relaunch.
locations.logistics: Ulica Rudolfa Kolaka 12, Zagreb; parking for production vehicles at Studio 2 and gated access with RF cards at the production hub.

locations.name: Plitvice Lakes National Park
locations.setting: Chain of sixteen terraced turquoise lakes linked by waterfalls in a forested karst canyon.
locations.known_for: Treasure of the Silver Lake (1962), Karl May Winnetou westerns (1962-1968)

locations.name: Archbishop's Palace, Kroměříž
locations.setting: UNESCO-listed baroque archbishop's palace with opulent state rooms and formal gardens that have stood in for imperial Vienna.

locations.name: Barrandov Studios
locations.setting: Prague studio complex dating from the early 1930s with large sound stages, extensive costume and prop stocks and backlot space.
locations.facilities: 14 soundproof stages totalling 10,900 m2 at Barrandov plus four at the Hostivar site, most with rigging pulley systems; permanent exterior sets include a 15,000 m2 medieval town with buildings up to 10 m and a 39 x 60 m Paris street with twenty facades and ten interiors. Production rooms, makeup and dressing rooms, wardrobe, camera and prop storage, catering spaces and a large costume and prop stock.
locations.suitability: Offers stage rental, set construction, costume and prop rental, dubbing and production support, with on-site firefighting services for pyrotechnics and high-risk scenes; the studio cites the Czech cash rebate of up to 35 percent.
locations.logistics: Barrandov site 10 minutes from Prague city centre and 15 minutes from Vaclav Havel Airport, Hostivar site 18 minutes from both; parking for cars and trucks on site. Website in Czech only.

locations.name: Český Krumlov
locations.setting: Renaissance and baroque town wrapped in a tight bend of the Vltava river beneath a painted castle tower.
locations.known_for: The Adventures of Pinocchio (1996), Hostel (2005), The Illusionist (2006)

locations.name: Christiansborg Palace
locations.setting: Government palace on the Slotsholmen islet housing the Danish Parliament, Prime Minister's Office and Supreme Court, with a riding ground complex and palace square.

locations.name: Kronborg Castle
locations.setting: Renaissance fortress at the narrowest point of the Øresund strait, with ramparts, a large courtyard and vaulted casemates, known as the Elsinore of Shakespeare's Hamlet.

locations.name: Nordisk Film Studios
locations.setting: Working studio lot in Valby founded in 1906, the world's oldest continuously active film studio, with shooting stages, post-production facilities and a 360-degree LED stage.
locations.facilities: 360-degree LED stage of 16 m diameter and 5.5 m height with LED walls and ceiling and an optional LED floor (ROE panels, up to 6,000 nits), run by Nordisk Film Shortcut; dressing rooms, makeup facilities and large parking for crew and grip trucks.
locations.suitability: The LED stage is offered for films, series, commercials, music videos and live events with virtual production supervision, Unreal Engine content, previs and driving plates; it takes vehicles, boats and planes up to 15 m. The stage runs on solar power from 2023.
locations.logistics: Mosedalvej 14, 2500 Valby, on the Nordisk Film lot; large parking for crew and grip trucks.

locations.name: Ivalo
locations.setting: Village on the Ivalo River about 250 kilometres north of the Arctic Circle, surrounded by boreal forest and fells, with deep snow and polar night for much of the year.

locations.name: Mediapolis
locations.setting: Media campus at broadcaster Yle's Tohloppi site in Tampere, with fully equipped television studios and a 1,500 square metre factory hall stage available for hire.
locations.facilities: Two Yle broadcast studios of 432 m2 (24 x 18 m) and 342 m2 (19 x 18 m) with tungsten lighting, hoists and 360-degree curtains; a 1,200 m2 Factory Hall (26 x 54.5 m, 10 m clear height); smaller TAMK and United studios of 133 and 198 m2; wardrobe and makeup rooms, six sound studios and edit stations.
locations.suitability: Studios are booked through a named contact per facility; the campus also offers production services, catering, event spaces and office facilities.
locations.logistics: 32,000 m2 campus in the Tohloppi district of Tampere where 1,000 to 1,100 people work and study daily

locations.name: Senate Square
locations.setting: Neoclassical square by Carl Ludvig Engel framed by Helsinki Cathedral, the Government Palace and the university, long used as a stand-in for imperial St Petersburg and Soviet-era Moscow.

locations.name: Cité du Cinéma (Studios de Paris)
locations.setting: Studio campus in a converted riverside power station with sound stages, workshops and offices around a monumental glass-roofed nave.
locations.known_for: Lucy, Valerian and the City of a Thousand Planets
locations.facilities: Nine sound stages from 6,506 to 22,271 sq ft (largest Stage 5, 201 x 111 ft, about 2,070 m2) with 47 to 52.5 ft to the grid; offices, artist green rooms with hair and makeup, VIP green rooms, workshops and storage.
locations.suitability: Stages offered with adjoining offices, green rooms, workshops and storage inside the Cite du Cinema campus; the site keeps a list of productions shot there.
locations.logistics: 20 rue Ampere, Saint-Denis: 30 minutes from Charles de Gaulle airport, 20 minutes from Le Bourget, 30 to 40 minutes from central Paris; served by RER D and metro lines 13 and 14 (direct to Orly), A86 and A1 motorway access, two four-star hotels a five-minute walk away.

locations.name: Étretat Cliffs
locations.setting: White chalk cliffs with natural arches and a freestanding needle rising above a pebble beach on the Alabaster Coast.

locations.name: Palace of Versailles
locations.setting: Baroque royal palace with the Hall of Mirrors, state apartments, vast formal gardens and two smaller palaces in the park.

locations.name: Alte Oper Frankfurt
locations.setting: Rebuilt 1880s opera house in Frankfurt, now a concert and congress venue with a restored historicist facade and a modern auditorium behind it.

locations.name: Autostadt Wolfsburg
locations.setting: Car-brand visitor park beside the Volkswagen plant in Wolfsburg, with pavilions, glass delivery towers, a museum hall and landscaped grounds beside a canal.

locations.name: Bauhaus Dessau
locations.setting: 1926 Bauhaus school building by Walter Gropius in Dessau, a UNESCO World Heritage site with glass curtain walls, workshop wings, studio flats and an auditorium.

locations.name: Bavaria Filmstadt
locations.setting: Working film studio complex in Grünwald near Munich with sound stages, a backlot and standing sets used for German film and television production since the 1920s.

locations.name: Beelitz-Heilstätten
locations.setting: Sprawling former tuberculosis sanatorium and military hospital south of Berlin with dozens of derelict Wilhelmine-era pavilions, overgrown grounds and a former alpine slide building.

locations.name: Berlin-Hohenschönhausen Memorial
locations.setting: Former Stasi remand prison in Lichtenberg with preserved interrogation rooms, cells and a prisoner transport van, run as a memorial site open for research and filming about East Germany.

locations.name: Deutsches Museum
locations.setting: Large science and technology museum on an island in the Isar in Munich, with historic machine halls, a planetarium and collections spanning mining to aerospace.

locations.name: Elbphilharmonie
locations.setting: Concert hall on the Elbe in Hamburg's HafenCity, built above a former cocoa warehouse with a glass wave-shaped upper structure, a public plaza and two auditoriums.

locations.name: Ferropolis
locations.setting: Open-air museum on a peninsula in a former lignite mining lake near Gräfenhainichen, displaying five giant excavators and dredgers on a bare industrial ground used for festivals and events.

locations.name: Frankfurt Bankenviertel
locations.setting: Frankfurt's financial district of glass office towers grouped around the old town and the river Main, the only high-rise skyline of its kind in Germany.

locations.name: Gasometer Oberhausen
locations.setting: 117-metre disused gas holder in Oberhausen converted into an exhibition hall, with a vast cylindrical interior used for large-scale installations.

locations.name: Görlitz Old Town
locations.setting: War-spared old town of around 4,000 listed buildings ranging from Gothic and Renaissance to Baroque and Wilhelminian styles.
locations.known_for: The Grand Budapest Hotel, Inglourious Basterds, The Reader

locations.name: Hamburg Rathaus
locations.setting: Neo-Renaissance city hall of 1897 on the Rathausmarkt in Hamburg, with a 112-metre tower, an ornate facade and several hundred rooms including ceremonial halls.

locations.name: Heidelberg University
locations.setting: Germany's oldest university, with a baroque Old University building, a Great Hall and a historic student prison around Universitätsplatz in Heidelberg's old town.

locations.name: Hellerau
locations.setting: Early twentieth-century garden city on the edge of Dresden built around the Hellerau Festival Theatre, with modernist workshop housing and a rhythmic-gymnastics hall used for performance and film.

locations.name: Humboldt University of Berlin
locations.setting: Berlin's oldest university on Unter den Linden, with a neoclassical main building, historic lecture halls, a courtyard and library reading rooms in the government district.

locations.name: Kampnagel
locations.setting: Former crane factory in Hamburg's Winterhude district converted into a production house for theatre, dance and performance, with large industrial halls and a forecourt.

locations.name: Kap Arkona
locations.setting: Northern tip of Rügen with two historic lighthouses, a former Cold War radar bunker and a reconstructed Slavic hillfort on chalk and boulder-clay cliffs above the Baltic.

locations.name: Kloster Eberbach
locations.setting: Former Cistercian monastery in the Rheingau with a Romanesque basilica, a vaulted dormitory, wine cellars and surrounding vineyards, now run as an events and wine estate.

locations.name: Kokerei Hansa
locations.setting: Former coking plant in Dortmund with intact coke oven batteries, coal towers, pump houses and machine halls preserved as an industrial heritage site.

locations.name: Königsstuhl (Rügen)
locations.setting: Chalk cliff on Rügen's Jasmund coast rising sharply above the Baltic, within a national park of beech forest, with a visitor centre built into the clifftop.

locations.name: Landschaftspark Duisburg-Nord
locations.setting: Disused early twentieth-century ironworks in Duisburg with blast furnaces, gasometers, bunkers and pipe bridges left standing in a public park, floodlit at night and open for climbing and diving.

locations.name: Lanxess Arena
locations.setting: Indoor arena in Cologne's Deutz district with a bowl seating around 20,000, used for concerts, ice hockey, basketball and television productions.

locations.name: Museum Park Rüdersdorf
locations.setting: Former limestone quarry and cement works east of Berlin preserved as an open-air museum, with quarry faces, kilns, a narrow-gauge railway and industrial machinery halls.

locations.name: Neuschwanstein Castle
locations.setting: Nineteenth-century Romanesque revival castle rising from a wooded Alpine crag above the village of Hohenschwangau.
locations.known_for: Chitty Chitty Bang Bang, The Great Escape, Ludwig (1973)

locations.name: Nürburgring
locations.setting: Motor racing circuit in the Eifel hills with the 20.8-kilometre Nordschleife loop and a separate shorter Grand Prix track, plus paddock, grandstands and a visitor centre.

locations.name: Olympiapark München
locations.setting: 1972 Olympic park in Munich with a tent-roofed stadium, hall and swimming venue around an artificial hill and lake, still used for concerts and sporting events.

locations.name: Panometer Leipzig
locations.setting: Former gasometer in Leipzig converted into a 360-degree panorama exhibition space, with a cylindrical brick interior more than thirty metres high.

locations.name: Peenemünde
locations.setting: Former Wehrmacht rocket research site on Usedom where the V2 was developed, with a preserved power station now housing a museum on wartime and Cold War history.

locations.name: Schauspielhaus Bochum
locations.setting: Repertory theatre in Bochum with a 1950s auditorium, stage house and rehearsal spaces, one of Germany's leading state theatres.

locations.name: Seebrücke Sellin
locations.setting: Pleasure pier of the Baltic resort of Sellin on Rügen, a rebuilt wooden and steel structure reaching out over the sea with a restaurant at its end.

locations.name: Spinnerei Leipzig
locations.setting: Former cotton mill in Leipzig's Plagwitz district, once continental Europe's largest, now a complex of galleries, artist studios and industrial halls around cobbled courtyards.

locations.name: Studio Babelsberg
locations.setting: The world's oldest large-scale film studio, in operation since 1912, with sound stages, workshops and permanent backlot sets.
locations.known_for: Metropolis, Inglourious Basterds, Bridge of Spies
locations.facilities: 21 sound stages totalling 300,000 sq ft on a 42-acre lot, largest Stage 20 at 75,826 sq ft (7,041 m2) and Stage 19 at 59,998 sq ft; indoor water tank of 500,000 litres and 4 m depth; 15,000 m2 Metropolitan Backlot with 54 facades of 12 to 15 m and 5,500 m2 of streets; exterior green screen wall, 9-acre open lot, set construction and a prop department with over a million items.
locations.suitability: Offers production services with internationally experienced crews, set construction, props and co-production and financing options; the backlot's four street sets can be dressed as Berlin, New York, London or Paris and carry vehicles up to 20 tonnes. Premises are not open to the public.
locations.logistics: August-Bebel-Strasse 26-53, Potsdam: from Berlin via the A115 to exit Potsdam-Babelsberg; S7 to Potsdam Hauptbahnhof or RE7 to Medienstadt Babelsberg (7-minute walk); from BER airport by RB22 to Griebnitzsee and bus 696.

locations.name: Stuttgart Hauptbahnhof
locations.setting: Stuttgart's main railway station, a 1920s stone terminus building with a tower, currently being converted into an underground through-station as part of the Stuttgart 21 project.

locations.name: Tempelhof Airport
locations.setting: Former Berlin city airport with a terminal building over a kilometre long, vast disused hangars and a 300-hectare former airfield now a public park, hired for filming, events and trade fairs.
locations.known_for: Bridge of Spies (2015), The Hunger Games: Mockingjay Part 2 (2015)

locations.name: Teufelsberg
locations.setting: Cold War listening station of geodesic radomes and control buildings on an artificial hill of wartime rubble in the Grunewald forest, with derelict interiors and open roof terraces.

locations.name: Völklinger Hütte
locations.setting: Disused nineteenth-century ironworks in Völklingen, a UNESCO World Heritage site with blast furnaces, ore bunkers, a power hall and elevated walkways through the plant.

locations.name: Weissenhofsiedlung
locations.setting: 1927 modernist housing estate on a Stuttgart hillside designed by Mies van der Rohe, Le Corbusier and other Weimar-era architects, with flat-roofed white houses, two of them open as a museum.

locations.name: Westfalenhallen
locations.setting: Exhibition and event complex in Dortmund with several linked halls, including a large arena hall, built from the 1920s onward and still used for trade fairs, sport and concerts.

locations.name: Wünsdorf Garrison Town
locations.setting: Former Wehrmacht and later Soviet military headquarters town near Zossen, with barracks, a domed former officers' club and rows of abandoned housing blocks.

locations.name: Zeche Zollern
locations.setting: Former colliery in Dortmund with an Art Nouveau machine hall, ornate portal building and preserved pit head machinery, run as part of the Westphalian Industrial Museum.

locations.name: Zeche Zollverein
locations.setting: Former coal mine and coking plant in Essen, a UNESCO World Heritage site with Bauhaus-style winding towers, coking ovens, conveyor bridges and vast industrial halls now used for exhibitions and events.

locations.name: Meteora
locations.setting: Byzantine monasteries perched on sheer sandstone rock pillars rising above the Thessalian plain.

locations.name: Nu Boyana Hellenic Film Studios
locations.setting: Purpose-built studio complex near Thessaloniki airport with eight sound stages totalling about 15,000 square metres and a 25,000 square metre backlot.

locations.name: Skopelos
locations.setting: Pine-fringed Aegean island with pebble coves, a whitewashed harbour town and the clifftop chapel of Agios Ioannis.

locations.name: Hungarian State Opera House
locations.setting: Miklós Ybl's neo-Renaissance opera house of 1884 on Andrássy Avenue, with a gilded horseshoe auditorium, marble staircases and an arcaded stone facade.

locations.name: Origo Studios
locations.setting: Purpose-built studio complex in Budapest with eleven stages, including nine soundstages and around 19,000 square metres of filming space, plus backlot areas and underwater filming facilities.
locations.facilities: 11 stages totalling over 19,000 m2: nine soundstages (largest Stage 6, 4,373 m2 and 20 m high; Stages 3 and 4, 2,662 m2 each) and two VFX stages with a 100 m2 greenbox; a 23 x 18.5 x 3 m water tank, 4-hectare backlot, about 4,000 m2 of production offices in four buildings with makeup and dressing rooms, and 8,409 m2 of warehouses and workshops in 15 units.
locations.suitability: Soundproofed, heated and air-conditioned stages with overhead grids and loading doors, offered for features, series, animation and documentaries; the studio cites the 30 percent Hungarian tax credit and runs on solar energy and district heating.

locations.name: Vajdahunyad Castle
locations.setting: Eclectic replica castle of 1896 on a lake island in Budapest's City Park, combining Romanesque, Gothic, Renaissance and Baroque wings within a few hundred metres.

locations.name: Reynisfjara
locations.setting: Black volcanic sand beach near Vík with hexagonal basalt columns, the Reynisdrangar sea stacks offshore and powerful Atlantic surf.
locations.known_for: Noah (2014), Rogue One: A Star Wars Story (2016)

locations.name: RVK Studios
locations.setting: Around 8,000 square metres of stages in a converted fertiliser plant at Gufunes, with three large studios a short drive from downtown Reykjavík.
locations.facilities: Three acoustically isolated stages of 2,775, 1,506 and 1,317 m2, all 16 m high, with 733 m2 of props and set storage next to Stage 1; dressing, makeup and wardrobe rooms, casting suites, open-plan and private offices, meeting rooms, a cafeteria and post-production with six edit suites and a 4K screening room.
locations.suitability: Full production services for films, series, commercials, music videos and photo shoots; stage floors take heavy loads and large access doors let vehicles inside. The studio cites Iceland's 25 to 35 percent rebate.
locations.logistics: Thengilsbas 14, Gufunes: a 7-minute drive from downtown Reykjavik, with parking on site and limited air traffic overhead.

locations.name: Svínafellsjökull
locations.setting: Heavily crevassed outlet glacier of Vatnajökull ending in a small lagoon, reachable in minutes from the Ring Road inside Vatnajökull National Park.

locations.name: Ardmore Studios
locations.setting: Ireland's longest-established film studios, offering sound stages, workshops and production offices on an 18-acre site in Bray.
locations.facilities: Eight sound stages from 3,000 to 23,250 sq ft (Stage F 23,250 sq ft at 21 ft high, Stage H 21,000 sq ft at 43 ft), over 120,000 sq ft of creative space with 25,000 sq ft of production offices and 57,000 sq ft of support space; a 120,000-litre underwater tank with camera pit in Stage A, workshops, backlot areas, hair and makeup, props and wardrobe departments.
locations.suitability: Self-contained, secure 18-acre site with drive-in access on selected stages, meeting rooms and secure broadband; the on-site team offers space planning for interior and exterior sets.
locations.logistics: Herbert Road, Bray, County Wicklow, 12 miles south of Dublin; ample parking on site.

locations.name: Kilmainham Gaol
locations.setting: Preserved nineteenth-century prison with a galleried Victorian east wing, stone corridors and bare exercise yards, now a museum.
locations.known_for: The Italian Job (1969), In the Name of the Father, Paddington 2

locations.name: Skellig Michael
locations.setting: Steep rocky island in the Atlantic off the Kerry coast, topped by a sixth-century monastic settlement of stone beehive huts.
locations.known_for: Star Wars: The Force Awakens, Star Wars: The Last Jedi

locations.name: Cinecittà
locations.setting: Historic Rome studio complex founded in 1937, with sound stages including the vast Teatro 5 and permanent backlot sets such as ancient Rome.
locations.known_for: Ben-Hur (1959), La Dolce Vita (1960), Rome (2005-2007, HBO/BBC)
locations.facilities: 22 soundstages (24 planned) from 380 to 3,500 m2, the largest Stage 22 (3,500 m2) and Stage 5 (2,880 m2), each with dressing rooms, offices, makeup rooms and workshops; an LED volume in Stage 18 with a 452 m2 curved wall (8 m high, 52 m long), a 417 m2 motorised ceiling and a 25 m rotating platform; a backlot of nearly 10 hectares with power and water and permanent sets, plus set construction, film lab and audio and video post-production.
locations.suitability: Stages are soundproof, air conditioned and many have waterproof trapdoors for effects; they can be booked individually or in combination. Five new soundstages and four renovations are announced for 2026.

locations.name: Sassi di Matera
locations.setting: Ancient cave-dwelling districts carved into a limestone ravine, frequently standing in for biblical-era Jerusalem.
locations.known_for: The Passion of the Christ (2004), Wonder Woman (2017), No Time to Die (2021)

locations.name: Villa del Balbianello
locations.setting: Eighteenth-century villa on a wooded promontory of Lake Como with terraced gardens and open lake panoramas, now a FAI heritage property.
locations.known_for: Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (2002), Casino Royale (2006)

locations.name: Fort Ricasoli
locations.setting: Vast 17th-century bastioned fort at the mouth of the Grand Harbour whose open parade grounds host large-scale open-air set builds.

locations.name: Malta Film Studios
locations.setting: State-run studio facility whose two vast exterior water tanks sit on the shoreline so their surfaces blend into the natural sea horizon, complemented by an indoor insert tank.
locations.known_for: Raise the Titanic (1980), U-571 (2000), Captain Phillips (2013)

locations.name: Mdina
locations.setting: Walled medieval hilltop city of narrow honey-coloured limestone streets, baroque palaces and a monumental main gate.

locations.name: Amsterdam Canal Ring
locations.setting: Seventeenth-century ring of tree-lined canals with gabled townhouses, humpback bridges and houseboats.
locations.known_for: The Fault in Our Stars, Ocean's Twelve

locations.name: Erasmusbrug
locations.setting: Asymmetric cable-stayed bridge with a 139-metre bent steel pylon spanning the Nieuwe Maas against the Rotterdam skyline.

locations.name: Media Park Hilversum
locations.setting: Television production campus in Hilversum with large audience studios such as Studio 21 and 22 and most national broadcasters on site.
locations.known_for: The Voice of Holland, The Voice Kids
locations.facilities: Studio 21 is offered as an event location with a 360 m2 LED screen, sound installation and light ceiling; the park houses over 100 media companies including NOS, RTL, NEP, EMG and ITV, with restaurants, a gym, a hair and makeup salon and childcare on site.
locations.suitability: A private business park without public opening hours; employees need a valid access pass and visitors are welcome around event start times. Studio specifications and rental terms are not published on the park's own site.
locations.logistics: Joop van den Endeplein 1, Hilversum: own railway station Hilversum Media Park with four trains an hour and a footbridge into the park; by car via A1 exit 9 Laren/Hilversum; 24-hour parking deck and garage A at EUR 2.00 per hour, card payment only.

locations.name: Atlantic Ocean Road
locations.setting: Eight-kilometre stretch of County Road 64 hopping between skerries on a chain of bridges, including the curved Storseisundet Bridge, exposed to open sea on both sides.

locations.name: Dagslys Studios
locations.setting: Five purpose-built stages from 81 to 500 square metres in Nydalen, Oslo, with lighting and grip rental, workshops, props storage and costume and makeup rooms in the same building.
locations.facilities: Five studios of 500, 211, 137, 124 and 81 m2 with shared makeup and costume fitting areas, showers, a dining space for 30, art department and props storage, a carpentry workshop and production offices; lighting, camera, generator and truck rental in the same building.
locations.suitability: Studios and equipment are rented for any media and film production, with 24-hour equipment delivery; part of Oslo Film Studios.

locations.name: Preikestolen (Pulpit Rock)
locations.setting: Flat granite cliff ledge about 600 metres above Lysefjord, reached only by a four-kilometre mountain hiking trail.

locations.name: Alvernia Studios
locations.setting: A domed studio complex near Krakow with multiple sound stages and a large blue-screen hall, built on a former limestone quarry site 18 kilometres from Krakow Airport.

locations.name: ATM Studio
locations.setting: Film and television production centre of around 14,000 square metres in Warsaw's Wawer district, with multiple soundstages, TV studios, production offices and post-production facilities.
locations.known_for: The Voice of Poland, Dancing with the Stars: Taniec z gwiazdami
locations.facilities: Six halls totalling 5,200 m2: Hall A 1,500 m2 (45 x 34 m, 12 m high), Halls B to E 800 m2 each (32 x 25 m, 6 to 7 m high) and Hall F 500 m2; 14 dressing rooms of 34 m2 and two VIP dressing rooms of 60 m2, eight makeup rooms, scenic warehouses of 110 to 440 m2, a 3,900 kg cargo lift, catering and conference rooms on a 14,000 m2 site.
locations.suitability: Offers set design and construction, lighting and sound, post-production and VFX, costume and prop rental, OB vans and a virtual studio; two 4 MVA transformer stations, per-hall power connections from 16 A to 400 A, fibre links for nationwide TV transmission and silent ventilation for sound recording. Quotes on request.
locations.logistics: Wal Miedzeszynski 384, Wawer district, about 12 km from Warsaw city centre; three independent parking areas.

locations.name: Centennial Hall
locations.setting: A UNESCO-listed 1913 reinforced-concrete domed hall in Wroclaw, seating up to 6,000 beneath a 42-metre ribbed concrete dome, set in surrounding park and garden grounds.

locations.name: EC1 Lodz
locations.setting: A former coal-fired power station of 1907 in central Lodz, restored as a science and culture centre with its original turbine hall, boiler house and control rooms intact.

locations.name: Gdansk Shipyard (European Solidarity Centre)
locations.setting: The historic Lenin Shipyard gate and slipways where the Solidarity movement began in 1980, bordered by the European Solidarity Centre's rusted-steel museum building and surviving shipyard halls.

locations.name: Hala Koszyki
locations.setting: A 1908 steel-framed market hall in Warsaw's Ochota district, restored behind its original facade into a food hall of restaurants, bars and shops around a glazed central nave.

locations.name: Hel Peninsula
locations.setting: A 35-kilometre sand spit enclosing the Bay of Gdansk, with pine-backed Baltic beaches on its open-sea side and a historic fishing town and former naval base at its tip.

locations.name: Historic Guido Coal Mine
locations.setting: A former working coal mine in Zabrze, now a branch of the Museum of Coal Mining, with underground tours down to 320 metres and a preserved pithead machine hall.

locations.name: Kasprowy Wierch Cable Car
locations.setting: A 1936 aerial cableway climbing from Kuznice to the 1,987-metre summit of Kasprowy Wierch in the Tatras, run in two stages with a mid-station at Myslenickie Turnie.

locations.name: Kazimierz, Kraków
locations.setting: Kraków's former Jewish quarter, where synagogues, cobbled lanes and tenement courtyards still follow the pre-war street layout.

locations.name: Manufaktura
locations.setting: Izrael Poznanski's 19th-century red-brick textile mill complex in Lodz, converted into a shopping, leisure and museum quarter around its original factory yard and chimney.

locations.name: Nikiszowiec
locations.setting: A brick workers' housing estate built 1908-1918 for the Giesche coal mine, its enclosed courtyard blocks, arcaded passages and communal bakery still inhabited today.

locations.name: Nowa Huta
locations.setting: A planned socialist-realist steelworkers' town built from 1949 beside the former Lenin steelworks, with a monumental central square, arcaded avenues and uniform apartment blocks.

locations.name: Ogrodzieniec Castle
locations.setting: Ruined 14th-century castle on the highest hill of the Kraków-Częstochowa Upland, its broken towers rising among limestone outcrops on the Trail of the Eagles' Nests.

locations.name: Opera Lesna (Sopot Forest Opera)
locations.setting: An open-air amphitheatre cut into wooded dunes above Sopot, seating around 4,300 beneath a part-covered stage, home to the annual Sopot Festival.

locations.name: ORP Blyskawica
locations.setting: A Grom-class destroyer launched in 1936 and preserved as a museum ship on Gdynia's waterfront, with its bridge, gun turrets and below-deck compartments open to visitors.

locations.name: Palace of Culture and Science
locations.setting: A 237-metre socialist-classicist tower built in 1955 as a gift from the Soviet Union, holding theatres, cinemas, a congress hall, museums and an observation deck over central Warsaw.

locations.name: PGE Narodowy
locations.setting: Warsaw's national stadium of 2011, built on the site of the former Tenth-Anniversary Stadium, with a retractable roof and a facade patterned on the Polish flag.

locations.name: Poznan Town Hall
locations.setting: A Renaissance town hall of 1560 on Poznan's Old Market Square, rebuilt to Italian designs, with an arcaded facade, a mechanical clock with butting goats and a council chamber now a history museum.

locations.name: Spodek
locations.setting: A saucer-shaped 1971 sports and concert arena in central Katowice, its suspended roof spanning a hall seating up to about 11,500 for events.

locations.name: Stadion Slaski
locations.setting: A bowl stadium built in 1956 on a reclaimed slag heap in Chorzow, rebuilt with a membrane roof and seating around 54,000 for football, speedway and concerts.

locations.name: Warsaw Uprising Museum
locations.setting: A former tram power station on Wola's Przyokopowa street, converted into a museum of the 1944 uprising, retaining its brick turbine hall and machinery among the exhibition spaces.

locations.name: Wieliczka Salt Mine
locations.setting: A working salt mine near Krakow dating to the 13th century, its tunnels reaching over 300 metres deep and including carved underground chapels and chambers open to visitors.
locations.known_for: On the Silver Globe (1988), Spellbinder: Land of the Dragon Lord (1997)

locations.name: Alfama
locations.setting: Lisbon's oldest quarter, a hillside maze of steep cobbled lanes, tiled facades and tram lines above the Tagus.

locations.name: Convento de Cristo
locations.setting: Templar castle and convent complex crowned by the round Charola oratory, with Manueline cloisters and hilltop ramparts above Tomar.
locations.known_for: The Man Who Killed Don Quixote (2018)

locations.name: Praia do Guincho
locations.setting: Wide Atlantic surf beach backed by dunes and the Sintra hills, known for strong wind and heavy waves.

locations.name: Almaden Mining Park
locations.setting: A former mercury mine in Ciudad Real with headframes, shafts and underground galleries open for visits, worked from Roman times until closure in 2001.

locations.name: Anden 0 (Chamberi Ghost Station)
locations.setting: A disused 1919 Madrid Metro station preserved with its original tiled advertisements and platform furniture, opened to the public as a small museum called Anden 0.

locations.name: Antigua Carcel de Segovia
locations.setting: A former provincial prison in Segovia's old town, its cell blocks and courtyard converted into a cultural and exhibition centre.

locations.name: Auditorio de Tenerife
locations.region: Santa Cruz de Tenerife, Canary Islands
locations.setting: A sail-shaped concert hall on the Santa Cruz de Tenerife waterfront designed by Santiago Calatrava, with a curved white concrete shell around the main auditorium.

locations.name: Azkuna Zentroa
locations.setting: A former wine and grain warehouse, the Alhondiga, in Bilbao rebuilt by Philippe Starck behind its original brick facade, with 43 varied columns under a rooftop pool and terrace.

locations.name: Bardenas Reales
locations.setting: A semi-desert badlands landscape in southern Navarre with eroded clay buttes, plateaus and canyons, crossed by marked tracks inside a managed nature reserve.

locations.name: Belchite (old town)
locations.setting: The ruined shell of a town destroyed in the 1937 Battle of Belchite, left standing as a memorial with intact facades, a bell tower and rubble-filled streets open to visitors.
locations.known_for: The Adventures of Baron Munchausen (1988), Pan's Labyrinth (2006)

locations.name: Bilbao Metro
locations.setting: A metro network known for Norman Foster's glass-tube station entrances, locally called fosteritos, running through Bilbao and under the Nervion estuary.

locations.name: Bombas Gens
locations.setting: A former water-pump factory in Valencia built in Art Deco style, its restored halls now an art foundation with gallery and workshop spaces.

locations.name: Camp Nou
locations.setting: FC Barcelona's stadium in the Les Corts district, one of Europe's largest football grounds, with tiered stands, a museum and tour access during redevelopment.

locations.name: Canfranc International Railway Station
locations.setting: A Beaux-Arts railway station in the Pyrenees built for a cross-border line to France, its platforms and grand hall largely disused since 1970 and now under partial restoration.

locations.name: City of Arts and Sciences
locations.setting: A cluster of white concrete and glass structures by Santiago Calatrava and Felix Candela beside the old Turia riverbed, including a planetarium dome, an opera house, a science museum and an oceanarium.

locations.name: City of Culture of Galicia
locations.setting: A hilltop complex of curved stone and glass buildings by Peter Eisenman above Santiago de Compostela, combining library, museum and archive functions on wide open plazas.

locations.name: Ciudad de la Luz
locations.setting: Purpose-built studio complex beside the Mediterranean on the edge of Alicante, with large sound stages, exterior water tanks and production support buildings, reopened to shoots in 2022.
locations.known_for: Asterix at the Olympic Games (2008), The Impossible (2012)
locations.facilities: Six sound stages from 1,620 to 2,340 m2 (Plato 3: 2,340 m2 and 2,000 kVA; Plato 4: 1,794 m2; Platos 1, 2, 5 and 6: 1,620 m2, 12.5 m high, 10 x 8 m door, 1,250 kVA), interior tanks in Platos 3 and 5; an exterior 100 x 80 m water tank (8,000 m2, 1.2 m base, 5.2 m in a 30 x 30 m pit, 120 x 12 m green screen) with an infinity horizon to the Mediterranean; Backlot 1 of 42,367 m2 and Backlot 2 of 75,246 m2, each with 4,000 kVA; production buildings, workshops, storage, auditorium and post-production.
locations.suitability: Stages have NC-25 acoustic insulation and silent air conditioning; the tank offers up to 16 m underwater visibility, wave and water cannon systems and fills in 48 hours. 24-hour private security and access control let production teams work at any hour.
locations.logistics: On the edge of Alicante; the site cites an international airport nearby and Madrid under two hours by AVE high-speed train.

locations.name: Ciudad Encantada
locations.setting: A karst rock park near Cuenca where erosion has carved limestone into towers and shapes along a signed walking route through pine forest.

locations.name: Complutense University of Madrid
locations.setting: A large 1930s university campus, Ciudad Universitaria, west of central Madrid, with monumental faculty buildings, an observatory and open lawns.

locations.name: Conde Duque
locations.setting: A former 18th-century army barracks in Madrid with a long baroque facade and large parade-ground courtyards, converted into a public cultural centre.

locations.name: Corralejo Dunes Natural Park
locations.setting: A protected dune field and beach on the north coast of Fuerteventura, with shifting white sand hills managed by the island council.

locations.name: Euskalduna Palace
locations.setting: A congress and concert hall in Bilbao built in weathered steel on the site of the former Euskalduna shipyard, its shape referencing a ship's hull under construction.

locations.name: Fabra i Coats
locations.setting: A former 19th-century textile mill in Barcelona's Sant Andreu district, its long brick sheds and chimney now used as artist studios and a cultural centre.

locations.name: Gran Teatre del Liceu
locations.setting: Barcelona's main opera house on La Rambla, with a gilded horseshoe auditorium, a grand foyer and a stage house rebuilt after a 1994 fire.

locations.name: Hospital de Sant Pau
locations.setting: A former working hospital in Barcelona built as a campus of Art Nouveau pavilions with domes, mosaics and underground connecting tunnels, now a monument and event venue.

locations.name: Las Medulas
locations.setting: A red-cliffed landscape left by Roman open-cast gold mining, honeycombed with tunnels and covered in chestnut trees, managed as a protected heritage site in the Bierzo hills.

locations.name: Matadero Madrid
locations.setting: A former municipal slaughterhouse and cattle market beside the Manzanares river, its early 20th-century brick pavilions converted into galleries, studios and event spaces.

locations.name: Mercado Central de Valencia
locations.setting: A 1928 Art Nouveau market hall in central Valencia with domed ceilings, stained glass and stalls trading under an iron and tile structure.

locations.name: Mercado de San Miguel
locations.setting: A restored early 1900s cast-iron and glass market hall next to Plaza Mayor in Madrid, now a covered food and tapas market.

locations.name: Mini Hollywood (Oasys Parque Tematico)
locations.setting: A preserved western film set in the Tabernas desert built for 1960s Spaghetti Westerns, with a saloon, jail and main street still used for stunt shows and shoots.
locations.known_for: A Fistful of Dollars (1964), For a Few Dollars More (1965)

locations.name: Museo del Ferrocarril de Madrid
locations.setting: Spain's railway museum, housed in the former Delicias terminus with its 19th-century iron and glass trainshed, displaying historic locomotives and carriages.

locations.name: Palacio de Cibeles / CentroCentro
locations.setting: Madrid's ornate former post office building on Plaza de Cibeles, now the city hall, with a public exhibition centre, a rooftop viewpoint and a domed central hall.

locations.name: Palau de la Musica Catalana
locations.setting: A Modernista concert hall in Barcelona by Lluis Domenech i Montaner, with a stained-glass skylight, sculpted facades and an ornate main auditorium.

locations.name: Playa de las Catedrales
locations.setting: A tidal beach at Ribadeo shaped by sea arches and cliffs up to 30 metres high, fully walkable only at low tide and reached with a free timed permit in summer.

locations.name: Plaza de Toros de Las Ventas
locations.setting: Madrid's Neo-Mudejar bullring seating over 23,000, with brick and ceramic tile facades, tiered stands and an on-site bullfighting museum.

locations.name: Real Alcázar of Seville
locations.setting: Mudéjar royal palace complex in central Seville with tiled courtyards, arched ceremonial halls and lush formal gardens.
locations.known_for: Lawrence of Arabia (1962), Kingdom of Heaven (2005), Game of Thrones (season 5, Dorne)

photo.author: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA. Edited by MenkinAlRire

locations.name: Riotinto Mining Park
locations.setting: An open-cast copper and mineral mining landscape in Huelva province with reddened terrain, a heritage mining railway and a mining museum.

locations.name: Royal Tapestry Factory
locations.setting: A working tapestry and carpet workshop in Madrid founded in 1721, still weaving on wooden looms in its original workshop halls, open for guided tours.

locations.name: Santiago Bernabeu Stadium
locations.setting: Real Madrid's stadium in central Madrid, seating over 80,000 under a retractable roof, with dressing rooms, a trophy room and pitch-level tour access.

locations.name: Soller Railway
locations.setting: A narrow-gauge heritage railway on Mallorca linking Palma to Soller through the Serra de Tramuntana, still running vintage wooden carriages dating from 1912.

locations.name: Tabakalera
locations.setting: A former state tobacco factory in San Sebastian, its early 20th-century industrial halls converted into a contemporary culture and creation centre.

locations.name: Tabernas Desert
locations.setting: Europe's only true desert, with eroded badlands, dry riverbeds and surviving western town sets from the spaghetti-western era.
locations.known_for: Lawrence of Arabia (1962), The Good, the Bad and the Ugly (1966), Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade (1989)

locations.name: Timanfaya National Park
locations.setting: A national park on Lanzarote covering volcanic terrain formed by 18th-century eruptions, with lava fields, craters and a visitor route by coach.

locations.name: Tower of Hercules
locations.setting: A still-operating Roman lighthouse on a headland outside A Coruna, the oldest lighthouse in continuous use in the world, refaced in granite in the 18th century.

locations.name: University of Alcala
locations.setting: A 16th-century university campus in Alcala de Henares, centred on the Colegio de San Ildefonso with its plateresque facade and a historic assembly hall.

locations.name: University of Salamanca
locations.setting: Spain's oldest university, with a 16th-century plateresque facade, cloisters and historic lecture halls set around Salamanca's old town.

locations.name: University of Seville (Rectorado)
locations.setting: Seville's university rectorate housed in the former Royal Tobacco Factory, an 18th-century industrial building with long stone facades, courtyards and vaulted halls.

locations.name: Vizcaya Bridge
locations.setting: A working transporter bridge over the Ria de Bilbao between Portugalete and Las Arenas, carrying a suspended gondola across the estuary since 1893, with a walkway on top.

locations.name: Fårö
locations.setting: Small Baltic island north of Gotland with limestone rauk stacks, shingle shores and windswept heathland, where Ingmar Bergman lived and filmed for decades.
locations.known_for: Persona (1966), Through a Glass Darkly (1961), Scenes from a Marriage (1973)

locations.name: Film i Väst
locations.setting: Regional film fund and studio base in Trollhättan, nicknamed Trollywood, whose stages and industrial halls have held full-scale purpose-built sets.
locations.price_note: Studio Fares SEK 25,000 for the first day and SEK 20,000 per following day, plus 25 percent VAT (own site)
locations.facilities: Studio Fares: one 1,100 m2 sound stage (31.3 x 36.1 m, 10 m to the gallery) with a telfer system of 40 hoists, 1,000 A permanent power plus 1,000 A temporary, and doors 4.5 m high; props storage, carpentry workshop, production offices with 26 desks on two floors, three dressing rooms, makeup and wardrobe and a 50-seat cafe with kitchen.
locations.suitability: Rented primarily to Film i Vast co-productions under a licence agreement; external bookings are accepted at most two months ahead. The rent includes utilities, parking, cleaning and use of the facilities.
locations.logistics: Trollhattan; gated, secure parking with four EV charging points. Website in Swedish only.

locations.name: Ystad
locations.setting: Medieval coastal town with half-timbered houses, cobbled streets and a sandy Baltic shoreline, home to the Ystad Studios film facility.

locations.name: Aerospace Bristol
locations.setting: Aviation museum on the former Filton airfield site with a hangar housing a preserved Concorde alongside earlier Bristol-built aircraft.

locations.name: Amberley Museum
locations.setting: Open-air industrial heritage museum on a former chalk quarry near Arundel, with narrow-gauge railways, a lime works, workshops and period industrial buildings.

locations.name: Audley End House and Gardens
locations.setting: Jacobean mansion near Saffron Walden remodelled in the eighteenth century, with state rooms, a service wing and Capability Brown parkland.

locations.name: Battersea Power Station
locations.setting: Decommissioned Thames-side coal power station with four white chimneys, its turbine halls and boiler house now restored inside a mixed-use redevelopment.
locations.known_for: The King's Speech, Children of Men

locations.name: Bodleian Library
locations.setting: Historic university library in central Oxford with the vaulted Divinity School and Duke Humfrey's medieval reading room, hired for filming by arrangement.
locations.known_for: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets

locations.name: Borough Market
locations.setting: Covered Victorian food market south of London Bridge with wrought-iron arcades, market stalls and surrounding cobbled streets.
locations.known_for: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Bridget Jones's Diary

locations.name: Bressingham Steam and Gardens
locations.setting: Steam preservation site near Diss with narrow-gauge railways, a collection of traction engines and steam locomotives, and surrounding show gardens.

locations.name: Bristol Old Vic
locations.setting: Working eighteenth-century theatre in central Bristol, one of the oldest continuously operating in the English-speaking world, with a Georgian auditorium and backstage spaces.

locations.name: Brooklands Museum
locations.setting: Site of the world's first purpose-built motor racing circuit near Weybridge, with a surviving banked track section, aircraft hangars and early aviation and motoring exhibits.

locations.name: Butser Ancient Farm
locations.setting: Open-air archaeological site near Chalton with reconstructed Iron Age roundhouses, a Roman villa and Anglo-Saxon buildings set in working farmland.

locations.name: Charlestown Harbour
locations.setting: Small Georgian-era dry-dock harbour near St Austell, still used by tall ships, with quayside cottages and period pilchard cellars around the basin.

locations.name: Cheddar Gorge
locations.setting: England's largest gorge, with 130-metre limestone cliffs, show caves and a clifftop footpath managed as part of the Longleat Estate.

locations.name: Cliveden
locations.setting: Italianate mansion above the Thames at Taplow, now a hotel, with formal parterre gardens, a walled garden and woodland grounds managed by the National Trust.

locations.name: Colne Valley Railway
locations.setting: Heritage standard-gauge railway on the Essex-Suffolk border with a rebuilt country station, signal box and steam and diesel locomotives.

locations.name: Dyrham Park
locations.setting: Baroque country house near Bath set in a steep deer park, with panelled state rooms, a Delftware collection and a walled garden.

locations.name: Eden Project
locations.setting: Environmental attraction built into a former china clay pit near St Austell, with two giant geodesic biome domes housing rainforest and Mediterranean planting.

locations.name: Elstree Studios
locations.setting: Film and television studio complex at Borehamwood with several sound stages, dating back to the 1920s and long used for major British productions.
locations.known_for: Star Wars, Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade

locations.name: Fort Amherst
locations.setting: Napoleonic-era fortification above Chatham with brick ramparts, gun batteries and a network of tunnels cut into the chalk.

locations.name: Freshwater West
locations.setting: Wide Atlantic surf beach backed by dunes and low cliffs on the open Pembrokeshire coast.
locations.known_for: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows: Part 1, Robin Hood (2010), Their Finest

locations.name: Fulham Palace
locations.setting: Moated former residence of the Bishop of London beside the Thames at Putney, combining Tudor courtyards, Georgian rooms and walled gardens available for filming.

locations.name: Geevor Tin Mine
locations.setting: Former working tin mine on the Cornish coast near Pendeen, with headframes, processing mills, underground tunnels and dressing floors preserved as a museum.

locations.name: Glenfinnan Viaduct
locations.setting: Curved 21-arch concrete railway viaduct of 1901 carrying the West Highland Line above the head of Loch Shiel.
locations.known_for: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban

locations.name: Hylands House
locations.setting: Neoclassical villa near Chelmsford set in landscaped parkland, with Regency reception rooms available for filming and events.

locations.name: Knole
locations.setting: Sprawling calendar house near Sevenoaks with medieval and Tudor courtyards, a deer park and largely unaltered seventeenth-century state rooms.

locations.name: Landguard Fort
locations.setting: Coastal artillery fort at the mouth of the River Orwell near Felixstowe, rebuilt in stages from the seventeenth to the twentieth century with gun casemates and magazines.

locations.name: Loseley Park
locations.setting: Elizabethan mansion near Guildford with panelled state rooms, a walled garden and surrounding parkland, hired for filming.
locations.known_for: Bridget Jones's Diary, The Wedding Date

locations.name: No.1 Royal Crescent
locations.setting: End-of-terrace Georgian townhouse on Bath's Royal Crescent, restored and furnished as a museum showing how it looked in the 1700s.

locations.name: Old Royal Naval College
locations.setting: Baroque waterfront complex of colonnaded courts and a domed Painted Hall at Greenwich, hired as a stand-in for period Paris, Victorian London and other settings.
locations.known_for: Bridgerton, The Crown, Les Misérables, Thor

locations.name: Orford Ness
locations.setting: Shingle spit on the Suffolk coast used for decades as a secret military testing site, with derelict laboratories, pagoda-shaped test buildings and a lighthouse.

locations.name: Pinewood Studios
locations.setting: Major studio complex west of London whose facilities include large sound stages, the vast 007 Stage, backlots and an underwater filming tank.
locations.known_for: No Time to Die, Star Wars: The Force Awakens
locations.facilities: 30 stages including the 007 Stage (59,092 sq ft, 5,490 m2, 12 m high, with a 91 x 22 m interior tank 2 m deep), an underwater stage with a 20 x 10 x 6 m tank of 1.2 million litres kept at 30 C, three backlots (Paddock Lot, North Lot) with a 32,000 sq ft water pad, workshops of 1,000 to 12,000 sq ft, production offices, hair and makeup rooms, six mixing theatres and 20 cutting rooms.
locations.suitability: Stages are hired individually or in combination; an Indie Film Hub keeps two stages for independent film, over 150 on-lot businesses supply equipment hire, motion capture and 3D scanning, and Diving Services UK manages the underwater stage. Canteen, bar, cinema and 24/7 security on the lot.
locations.logistics: Pinewood Road, Iver Heath: 10 miles from Heathrow, via M4 junction 5 or A40 junction 1; about 45 minutes from Baker Street by Underground to Uxbridge then 10 minutes by taxi, with a free shuttle bus to Uxbridge, Slough, Gerrards Cross and West Ruislip stations; on-site parking.

locations.name: Portsmouth Historic Dockyard
locations.setting: Working Royal Navy dockyard and heritage site with historic warships, dry docks and Georgian storehouses along Portsmouth Harbour.

locations.name: Royal Albert Hall
locations.setting: Circular Victorian concert hall with a domed glass and iron roof, tiered galleries and a large stage, available for filming and photography by arrangement.
locations.known_for: The Man Who Knew Too Much, The King's Speech

locations.name: Royal Holloway, University of London
locations.setting: Victorian university campus at Egham centred on the ornate French Renaissance-style Founder's Building, with quadrangles, a chapel and a picture gallery.

locations.name: Shepton Mallet Prison
locations.setting: Former English prison dating to 1610, closed in 2013, with cell wings, exercise yards and a gatehouse now hired as an events and filming venue.

locations.name: Snape Maltings
locations.setting: Former Victorian malting complex on the River Alde, its brick maltings and kilns converted into a concert hall, galleries and shops.

locations.name: Somerset House
locations.setting: Neoclassical courtyard building on the Strand with a fountain court and river terrace, hired for events and productions in central London.

locations.name: Southwold Pier
locations.setting: Traditional seaside pier rebuilt in the 2000s on its Edwardian footings, with a pavilion, amusement arcade and end-of-pier walkway over the North Sea.

locations.name: SS Great Britain
locations.setting: Preserved Victorian iron-hulled steamship in her original dry dock in Bristol, with restored decks, engine room and dockside museum buildings.

locations.name: The Historic Dockyard Chatham
locations.setting: 80-acre former Royal Navy dockyard on the Medway with Georgian ropewalks, covered slips, dry docks and historic ships used as period maritime backdrops.

locations.name: The Old Truman Brewery
locations.setting: Former East End brewery complex on Brick Lane with converted vat rooms, yards and warehouse floors hired as event and shoot space.

locations.name: The Tank Museum
locations.setting: Military vehicle museum on the Bovington army camp with several hundred tanks and armoured vehicles, indoor halls and outdoor arena space.

locations.name: Tower Bridge
locations.setting: Bascule and suspension bridge over the Thames with twin Victorian Gothic towers and a glass-floored high-level walkway overlooking the city.
locations.known_for: The Mummy Returns, Spider-Man: Far From Home

locations.name: Trinity Buoy Wharf
locations.setting: Former lighthouse testing wharf at the mouth of the River Lea, with a lightship, converted shipping-container studios and dockside sheds.

locations.name: Two Temple Place
locations.setting: Neo-Gothic mansion built for William Waldorf Astor beside the Thames, with a galleried great hall and carved wood interiors offered for filming.

locations.name: Wilton's Music Hall
locations.setting: Surviving Victorian music hall in Wapping with a barley-twist column auditorium and worn brick backstage areas, hired for filming and photography.

locations.name: Wrest Park
locations.setting: Country house near Silsoe built in French chateau style, set within formal gardens with canals, pavilions and woodland walks.
